0.original: Thiuna appears to be deep in thought.

49.original: Uwaaah! H-How long have you been standing there? I was so deep in thought, I didn't notice you.

50.original: You see, I've been pondering whether to speak with you about Owell. That you should appear at this moment is a sign. Please hear me.

51.original: As you know, Owell and I were orphans taken in by Master Harig.

52.original: We were close friends, playing and arguing with one another in turn, and together we trained as artisans. But all of that changed when Master Harig disappeared.

53.original: Young as we were then, we weren't told what became of him. But it's more than likely that, like so many others, he was slain by a sin eater.

54.original: From that time on, Owell and I drifted apart. Eventually we stopped speaking entirely. It was only when I announced my intention to open my shop that he had words for me, and they were none too kind. “You don't understand anything,” he spat out angrily.

55.original: Well, he's right in one regard. I don't understand why he so detests my work. It goes beyond mere disapproval. He makes it personal, as if I've done something to offend him.

56.original: This wouldn't be a problem, except Owell holds considerable influence at the Mean. A bad word from him and we would get no more custom. Sooner or later, I'll have to settle our differences, but the mere anticipation of it is nerve-racking. Ah, what I wouldn't give for a stiff drink...

57.original: <blip> Command received. <bloop> Instruction to Thiuna: proceed to the Wandering Stairs.

59.original: Oh no, Noddy's going to summon Owell!

60.original: <sigh> Seems it's to be sooner than later... <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>, might I ask you to join me at the Wandering Stairs? I could use the support.

62.original: Owell isn't here yet. I wouldn't be surprised if he doesn't come at all.

63.original: Thiuna. So you're the “urgent business” that I had to drop everything for.

64.original: Affirmative! <buzz> Thiuna has a score to settle with you!

68.original: There's something I need to ask you, Owell.

69.original: Make it quick. Unlike you, I've got responsibilities.

70.original: All right. Not everyone agrees with what I do. I understand that. What I don't understand is why you're so angry with me.

71.original: You called me here just to ask me <hex:021A020203>that<hex:021A020103>? Hah, urgent business indeed! How easy life must be when your days are filled with play!

72.original: What we do isn't play! We restore those items that hold sentimental value for the people of the Crystarium!

74.original: Thanks to the efforts of our ancestors, we've come to enjoy a semblance of a normal life. But shortages are still a daily reality.

75.original: Shortages you do nothing to alleviate! In the time it took you to restore a single decrepit set of amaro barding, I crafted a dozen new ones!

76.original: With Master Harig gone, it falls to me to prop up the Mean.

77.original: It falls to me because Master had to go off to satisfy some vain obsession...and you had to take after him!

79.original: <bloop> Resuming suspended operations. Owell not detected. Shall I fetch him?

81.original: I'm sorry you had to witness that, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. Owell...he didn't use to be that way.

82.original: While I believe in what we do, I can't deny that there's truth to his words. But hmmm... “Go off to satisfy an obsession”...

83.original: The day Master Harig disappeared, he had ventured out to procure materials. The item he was seeking to restore was... Ah.

84.original: <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>, I hate to involve you in my personal dilemmas, but I need your help. Can I rely on you?

85.original: I'm truly grateful. Let's return to the Crystalline Mean. I'll explain everything there.

86.original: <blip> Retrieving profile for Owell. <bloop> A Hume male, Owell is an artisan of the Facet of Crafting. Marital status: single. Favorite beverage: hot milk.

87.original: If Cherished Memories is to survive, we must do something to stem Owell's criticism.

88.original: He's already done damage to our reputation, judging by the recent decline in business.

89.original: We must win him over somehow. Convince him that Cherished Memories is a serious venture, and make him see the true worth of restoration.

90.original: With regards to the latter, I have an idea. There's an item which, if restored, is bound to strum on Owell's heartstrings.

91.original: But I'm at a loss as to how we might show him that we mean business...

93.original: Ignore the criticism and let our work speak for us.

96.original: Would that we could, but Owell holds too much influence. We have to do something to make him change his mind about us.

97.original: Hmmm, now that you mention it, our workshop doesn't have much to draw the eye. Perhaps there's something to be said for looking the part...

98.original: Hmmm? What are you implying about my adorable assistant, pray tell?

99.original: <blip> In order to advertise their presence, shops commonly make use of signage. At present, Cherished Memories has none.

100.original: Of course! A sign! Why didn't I think of that?

101.original: <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>, would you be willing to fashion a sign for our workshop?

102.original: In light of all the help you've given us, it seems only right that you have the honor.

103.original: Thank you so much! I can't wait to see the finished product. Oh, and if you run out of materials, Noddy will furnish you with more.

104.original: <blip> I have more materials should you require them.

105.original: <blip> Analyzing sign... <buzz> Mmm-hmmm, very nice. I do not know much about signs, but I know what I am programmed to like.

106.original: How fares work on the sign? I can't wait to see it!

107.original: Blessed night, what a magnificent sign this is! It incorporates all the techniques of our restoration work─a perfect representation of who we are! From the design to the details, everything about it is wonderful!

108.original: Not only will this sign attract customers, it will serve to remind me of my goal to emulate your skills. I can't thank you enough for it.

109.original: With this, we can finally show Owell that we mean business.

110.original: I'll see to hanging the sign up as soon as possible. It's bound to be the envy of other artisans!

111.original: All that remains, then, is to impress upon Owell the true worth of restoration. On which front, there's something I would show you.

112.original: This lute was a gift from the Exarch to Master Harig. Since he left us, it has lain there, broken and silent.

113.original: Apparently, it was an enchanted instrument whose power had long faded, but its tone was no less beautiful for it.

114.original: Master would often play this lute at the tavern, and Owell and I would go and listen. Seeing how keen we were, he even gave us lessons.

115.original: We loved the rich, soothing sound, and we weren't alone. Whenever Master Harig played, the tavern was always full.

116.original: No matter how rowdy the patrons were, as soon as the first chord was strummed, a hush would fall over the place. The music resonated with them, filling their hearts with peace in both good times and in bad.

117.original: <blip> Following Harig's disappearance, however, the lute has been gathering dust.

118.original: W-Well, that's because no one could restore it properly save Master himself. An instrument demands consummate skill. Back then it was completely beyond me, and even now I don't feel equal to the task.

119.original: But I must try. Master wouldn't want to see Owell and I quarreling. No, he'd want us to join hands and serve the Crystarium and her people.

120.original: As it does for me, the lute holds fond memories for Owell. By restoring it, I'm hopeful that we can reach out to him.

121.original: <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>, this time it's a personal request. I need your help to make this lute sing once more.

122.original: Thank you. It gives me heart to have your support. I'll make ready for the restoration and let you know what I require.

123.original: The next request will be available from Thiuna upon reaching level 78 as a carpenter, leatherworker, or weaver.
